solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old provincial governor finally senses an ambush

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word senses

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
an ambush is a trap laid for the unwary

explanation.surface: An ancient governor, at the last moment, senses that he is walking into an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a regional ruler of a province in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Thus American spies left an informal gathering

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: US agents slip away from a casual party.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a friendly get-together, such as a club evening.

clue.text: Broadcast game, behold, in US state

indicators.note: broadcast means the name of the game is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: tennis is a game played with racquets
behold means see or look

explanation.surface: A televised sports match takes place in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, TENNIS gives the first syllables TENNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty United States, home of Nashville.

clue.text: Gave vent to anger in commercial

indicators.note: in places the word for anger within the word for a commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone let off steam furiously during a TV advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a grievance is to voice it openly, the same as giving vent to it.

clue.text: Mellow sound made by farm animal in south

indicators.note: in places the cow's noise inside the abbreviation for the compass point

parts.note: STH is a standard abbreviation for south
a cow's call is a moo

explanation.surface: A soft lowing from a cow down in the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A mellow wine or voice is smooth: free of harshness, gentle on the palate or ear.

clue.text: Italian physicist taking brandy on island

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings

explanation.surface: A scientist from Italy drinking brandy on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian physicist who pioneered radio transmission.

clue.text: Sash originally bought in old India

indicators.note: in sets the initial inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word bought

explanation.surface: A sash first purchased in India under British rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn round the waist with a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Mountaineer forks out pounds for a term at Oxford

indicators.note: forks out reads as paying, but here means taking out the money abbreviation

parts.note: Sir Edmund Hillary made the first ascent of Everest in 1953
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A climber pays for a stretch of study at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forks out' tempts as 'pays', but it signals removing L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary term is the spring academic term at Oxford, running January to March.

clue.text: Disputed claim initially about balls bowled in test

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word claim

parts.note: about in the sense 'concerning' gives ON

indicators.note: in sets the cricket term inside the word for a test

parts.note: a trial is a test
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so balls bowled are overs

explanation.surface: A cricket appeal about some deliveries in a Test match is hotly contested.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a Test is an international match and an over is a set of six deliveries; here 'test' just means TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something controversial is the subject of public dispute and argument.

clue.text: Signaller's device weighing practically nothing?

definitions.meaning: a coloured flare fired from a pistol as a signal
... literally means of almost no weight

explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a signalling flare named after its inventor, Edward Very; read literally, it means hardly heavy at all.

clue.text: Alter the last word at end of screed

parts.note: amen is the word that closes a prayer, so it is the last word

indicators.note: at end of selects the final letter of the word screed

explanation.surface: An editor tweaks the closing word of a long written rant.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to change or correct it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Aussie native's short word for male fowl

parts.note: the kangaroo, an Australian native animal, is shortened to roo, here with the possessive 's

indicators.note: short means the synonym for word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a word

explanation.surface: An Australian's abbreviated name for a cockerel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is the usual American and Australian name for a cock, an adult male chicken.

clue.text: Exercise machine reforming team drill

indicators.note: reforming means forming the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: A gym device for getting the squad back into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a moving-belt machine used for walking or running indoors.

clue.text: Plot involving a legendary archer's sidekick

indicators.note: involving means the plot word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a plot of land is a site
William Tell, the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: A scheme that drags in the faithful companion of a famous bowman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme but is a piece of ground, SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a follower or dependent hanger-on, figuratively orbiting a more important person.

clue.text: Bar coated with the right solvent

indicators.note: coated with means the pub word is wrapped by the other letters

parts.note: an inn is a bar or pub

explanation.surface: A bar is covered with the proper chemical for cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinner is a solvent added to paint to dilute it.

clue.text: Stick one's nose in, hearing gong?

indicators.note: hearing says the word is to be taken by how it sounds

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: Prying when you hear a dinner gong sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere in other people's affairs, the idiom of poking one's nose in.

clue.text: Woman breaks record, being the worse for wear

indicators.note: breaks means the woman's name splits the record abbreviation

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a record
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman sets a new record while badly hungover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks record' suggests a sporting feat; 'breaks' is the insertion signal, and 'the worse for wear' here means drunk, not shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned is slang for drunk, and being the worse for wear can mean intoxicated.

clue.text: Levelling out late in the day

definitions.meaning: ..., from even, means making level or smooth
the later part of the day, after afternoon

explanation.surface: Things calming down as the day draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the time after the afternoon; the verb form means making something flat or equal.

clue.text: Woman identified in ghastly diatribe

indicators.note: identified in says the name can be picked out within the next two words

explanation.surface: A woman is named in a horrible tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name, so a woman is a fair general definition.

clue.text: Study Latin at first and make money

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word Latin

parts.note: to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: Begin with studying Latin and then go out to make a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to study and acquire knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: March exhibition

definitions.meaning: a march is a protest procession
a showing of how something works, an exhibition

explanation.definitionFit: A protest march and a practical display are both called demonstrations.

clue.text: Encountered leaders in Middle Eastern territory

indicators.note: leaders in takes the front letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Bumped into heads of state in a region of the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Met is the past tense of meet, so it means came across or encountered.

clue.text: Complete set of books kept in European republic

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of volumes stored somewhere in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete set' reads as one phrase, but 'Complete' is the definition and 'set of books' is NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and complete both mean whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Early settler finally relaxed and fished

parts.note: the Angles were Germanic people who settled in England in the 5th century

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word relaxed

explanation.surface: A pioneer at last unwound and went fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line, so angled is past tense for fished.
